method: Ten real oncology patent documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. Every structure was located by reading the PDF itself - pdftotext -layout and pdfimages -png where the document has a text layer, pdftoppm page renders at 100-250 dpi where it does not (six of the ten are full-page raster scans with zero extractable text). Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: a PubChem PUG-REST lookup keyed on something PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT (an INN, a full IUPAC name, a CAS number, or - in the niraparib patent - the molecular weight printed under each drawing), AND a reading of the drawing itself. Where the document prints no name, the SMILES read off the drawing was submitted to PUG-REST /compound/smiles/ and accepted only when the returned InChIKey matched the hand reading exactly. Every SMILES round-trips through RDKit Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and its InChIKey was recomputed with RDKit and checked against PubChem's. Per-molecule `confidence` is name_match, drawing_read, generic or unresolved. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true), open-valence substituent fragments, resin-bound solid-phase species, variable-stoichiometry co-crystals, and structures with no second independent view (confidence: unresolved). Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row.
count_caveat: structures_drawn counts DEPICTIONS and is EXACT - counted box by box at 150-250 dpi - for EP2736895B1_osimertinib, EP3630761B1_sotorasib, US12011442B2_abemaciclib, WO2021259732A1_zanubrutinib, WO2017215166A1_talazoparib. It is an ESTIMATE from a 40-110 dpi contact sheet for US11629137B2_niraparib, CN114085213A_vepdegestrant, WO2025055671A1_elacestrant, US9463252B2_auristatin_MMAF, US12018032B2_icovamenib, each of which says so in its own `note`. No estimated count can move a score: recall is computed over `molecules` and precision over what a pipeline emits, and both of those are exact. The five estimated groups should be scored recall-only in any case, because most of what they draw is uncatalogued.

NOTE the depiction feature that makes it worth listing: the Fig. 33 drawing on p41 prints NUMBERED ATOM POSITIONS (1, 3, 4, 6, 13, 14, 16, 18-20, 23-25, 27, 32-34, 36, 37, 39, 40) directly on the skeleton, so stray digits sit inside the structure box.

unscoreable.name: deuterated analogues of Compound A and Compound P
unscoreable.label: deuterium analogue series
unscoreable.note: About twenty structures across pp81-84, each Compound A or Compound P with explicit 'D' atom labels at a DIFFERENT subset of positions - the morpholine ring, the pyrrole CH, the acrylamide vinyl, the piperidine, the central pyridine. The surrounding text enumerates the subsets in words ('deuterium is attached to any one or more positions selected from 13 and 15 as shown above'), so many of the depictions are members of a described SET rather than single compounds, and none is named. This is the same depiction class as the round-4 deutetrabenazine patent US8524733B2, at four times the density and with the deuteration pattern varying box to box.

US12018032B2_icovamenib.count_semantics: structures_drawn counts DEPICTIONS on the page. structures_resolved / structures_generic / structures_unresolved count ROWS in this group - distinct compounds or, for the unresolved ones, named classes of depiction. The four do not sum, and are not meant to, for the same reason pdf_manifest_round34.json's do not: a compound drawn twenty-six times is one row.
